headline: Bruins get steamrolled in Minnesota as Patriots head to Buffalo
morning_brew: Saturday night in Minnesota was a total disastah. The B's managed one goal early from Tanner Jeannot and then basically checked out, giving up four unanswered to the Wild. Watching the ice tilt toward Michael DiPietro for the final forty minutes was brutal, and you have to wonder if this group is still finding their legs after a quick start to the year. A loss like this hurts when you expect a better defensive showing.

The headlines don't get any easier for the Hub. With the Bruins trying to regroup before Monday's date with the Senators at the Garden, the real stress today is in western New York. The Patriots are walking into Highmark Stadium for a one o'clock kickoff against the Bills, and the status of our defensive unit is the only thing on my mind. We are facing a division rival on their own turf, and if we want to move past that tough start, we need to show some serious teeth today.

I haven't seen a secondary unit look this thin since cousin Jimmy tried to coach his own intramural squad. We've got work to do across the board, and the margin for error is shrinking by the hour. Kickoff is at one and my stomach is already in knots, so let's hope the Pats come out swinging because a win in Buffalo would do wonders for the mood around town.

news_digest.headline: Senators visit the Bruins in Atlantic Division action
news_digest.dans_take: A prime chance to wash that nasty Minnesota taste right out of our mouths on Monday.

news_digest.headline: Patriots preach patience when it comes to receiver WR Romeo Doubs' modest start
news_digest.dans_take: Patience is a luxury we don't have with the Bills staring us down on the schedule.
